'''Arts and culture'''
*Events affected by the COVID-19 pandemic, [[COVID-19 pandemic in Taiwan]]
**[[Taiwan]] cancels the upcoming [[Taiwan Lantern Festival]] for the first time since 1990, due to an increase in [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases on the island. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/taiwan-cancels-major-festival-as-domestic-covid-19-cases-rise (''The Straits Times'')]

'''Business and economy'''
*The [[National Highway Traffic Safety Administration]] of the United States orders [[Ford Motor Company]] to [[Product recall|recall]] about three million of its vehicles containing [[airbag]]s manufactured by [[Takata Corporation|Takata]], citing "potential future rupture risks". [https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/transport/us-orders-ford-to-recall-3-million-vehicles-with-takata-airbags (AFP via ''Business Times'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Fifteen people are killed by a truck in [[Surat]], [[India]] while they were sleeping by a road. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/1/19/more-than-a-dozen-sleeping-workers-crushed-under-truck-in-india (Al Jazeera English)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York (state)]]
*****[[COVID-19 pandemic in New York City]]
******[[Andrew Yang]], a candidate for [[Mayor of New York City|Mayor]] of [[New York City]] in the [[2021 New York City mayoral election|upcoming mayoral election]], will quarantine after one of his staffers tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2021/01/19/nyregion/andrew-yang-coronavirus.html (''The New York Times'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Vermont]]
*****[[Vermont]] [[Governor of Vermont|Governor]] [[Phil Scott]], Health Commissioner Mark Levine, and other officials quarantine after a contractor that Levine was in contact with tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.mynbc5.com/article/vermont-governor-health-commissioner-in-quarantine-after-possible-covid-19-exposure/35258382 (WPTZ-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****A memorial at the [[Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool]] is held, honoring the 400,000 [[Americans]] who have died as a result of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. Additionally, bells are rung at the [[Washington National Cathedral]] and a moment of silence is held. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-health-coronavirus-usa/bells-and-candlelight-to-honor-400000-covid-19-dead-on-eve-of-us-presidential-handover-idUSKBN29O24X (Reuters)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/joe-biden-deliver-remarks-pandemic-u-s-tops-400-000-n1254746 (NBC News)]
****The [[United States]] surpasses 400,000 deaths from [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]], just five weeks after passing 300,000 deaths. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-19-death-toll-400k-united-states/ (CBS News)] [https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/01/19/957488613/as-death-rate-accelerates-u-s-records-400-000-lives-lost-to-the-coronavirus (NPR)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mexico]]
****[[Mexico]] reports a record 1,584 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to nearly 143,000. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/mexico-reports-new-one-day-record-of-1584-covid-19-deaths/2021/01/19/bca0c650-5ac1-11eb-a849-6f9423a75ffd_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Portugal]]
****[[Portugal]] reports a new record for the second consecutive day, of 218 deaths, bringing the nationwide death toll to 9,246. At the same time, the nationwide number of ICU patients reaches a record 670, just below the maximum allocation capacity of 672 ICU beds set the day before. [https://covid19.min-saude.pt/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/323_DGS_boletim_20210119.pdf (DGS)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/idUSP4N28Q028 (Reuters)]
****Portuguese [[Ministry of Economy (Portugal)|Economy Minister]] [[Pedro Siza Vieira]] tested positive for [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]]. [https://www.tsf.pt/portugal/politica/pedro-siza-vieira-esta-infetado-com-covid-19-13251491.html (TSF)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Andorra]]
****The first 30,000 doses of the [[Pfizer]]-[[BioNTech]] vaccine are sent from [[Spain]] to [[Andorra]] after both governments reached an agreement earlier today. [https://www.euroweeklynews.com/2021/01/19/spain-plans-sell-30000-doses-covid-vaccine-andorra/ (Euro Weekly News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Germany]]
****[[Chancellor of Germany|Chancellor]] [[Angela Merkel]] and the leaders of all 16 [[States of Germany|states]] agree to extend the nationwide [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] until February 14, due to the threat of [[Variants of SARS-CoV-2|new variants of SARS-CoV-2]]. They also agree to mandate [[medical mask]]s for all passengers on public transport. [https://www.tagesschau.de/inland/beschlussvorlage-corona-105.html (Taggeschau)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland]]
****[[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] reports a record 93 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 2,708. [https://www.irishexaminer.com/news/arid-40210295.html (''Irish Examiner'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] reports a record 1,610 deaths in the past 24 hours, bringing the nationwide death toll to 91,470. [https://www.itv.com/news/2021-01-19/covid-uk-records-1610-more-coronavirus-deaths-the-highest-daily-figure-since-pandemic-began (ITV)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Hong Kong]]
****[[Hong Kong]] extends their [[work from home]] arrangements for [[civil servant]]s until January 27, as the city attempts to reduce the number of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] cases. [https://financialpost.com/pmn/business-pmn/hk-govt-extends-work-from-home-for-civil-servants-until-jan-27 (Reuters via ''Financial Post'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Israel]]
****[[Israel]] extends their third nationwide lockdown until January 31 as the country reports its highest number of cases since the pandemic began. They will also require all travelers to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test result]] within 72 hours of arrival or face a fine of [[Israeli new shekel|NIS]] 2,500 ($772). [https://www.timesofisrael.com/government-extends-lockdown-until-january-31-amid-soaring-virus-rates/ (''The Times of Israel'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****The [[Shizuoka Prefecture|Shizuoka]] [[prefectures of Japan|prefectural]] government issues an emergency alert after three cases of the more contagious variant from the UK are reported in people with no known travel history. [https://english.kyodonews.net/news/2021/01/998de4b50134-shizuoka-pref-issues-emergency-alert-over-new-coronavirus-variant.html (Kyodo News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]], [[Variant of Concern 202012/01]]
****[[Kuwait]] reports their first cases of the B.1.1.7 variant of [[Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2|SARS-CoV-2]] in two women who travelled from the [[United Kingdom]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/gulf/kuwait/kuwait-reports-two-cases-of-new-covid-19-variant-1.76590091 (Gulf News)] 
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Malaysia]]
****[[Malaysia]]'s Senior Minister [[Ismail Sabri Yaakob]] announces the extension of the second [[Malaysian movement control order|movement control order]] to six states from January 22 at 12:01 a.m. local time until February 4. This means that all [[States and federal territories of Malaysia|states and federal territories]] except [[Sarawak]] will be placed under tighter restrictions. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/asia/malaysia-covid-19-mco-all-states-except-sarawak-jan-22-feb-4-13993694 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
***The [[New Zealand government]] imposes a mandatory requirement for all travellers to present a negative [[COVID-19 testing|COVID-19 test result]] before departing for [[New Zealand]], beginning January 25. This requirement does not include residents of [[Australia]], [[Antarctica]] and most Pacific Island countries. [https://www.nzherald.co.nz/nz/covid-19-coronavirus-government-extends-pre-departure-tests-to-more-travellers/HWRVBKWOXJBMTQIYQNAS62YZOU/ (''NZ Herald'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Uganda–United States relations]]
**A [[Ugandan government]] spokesman accuses the [[U.S. government]] of "[[subversion]]" after [[ambassador]] [[Natalie E. Brown]] tried to visit opposition leader [[Bobi Wine]] at his home, where he is under [[house arrest]]. Brown said that she wanted to check on the "health and safety" of Wine. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-uganda-election/uganda-accuses-u-s-of-subversion-after-envoy-tries-to-visit-wines-house-idUSKBN29O0FZ?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[China–United States relations]], [[Uyghur genocide]]
**The outgoing [[First presidency of Donald Trump|Trump administration]] declares that [[China]] has committed [[Uyghur genocide|genocide]] against [[Uyghurs|Uyghur]] Muslims and other ethnic minority groups. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/china-sanctions-uighur-muslims-genocide-mike-pompeo/ (CBS News)]
  
'''Law and crime'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
**[[Grafton vaccine incident]], [[COVID-19 pandemic in Wisconsin]]
***[[Wisconsin]] pharmacist Steven Brandenburg is charged with attempted misdemeanor property damage for deliberately trying to defrost doses of [[Moderna]]'s [[Moderna COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]]. [https://apnews.com/article/health-milwaukee-wisconsin-coronavirus-pandemic-9443605e57f9129e11068ed80ecd2d89 (AP)]
*[[Aftermath of the January 6 United States Capitol attack|Aftermath of the 2021 storming of the United States Capitol]]
**Three members of the [[Oath Keepers]] far-right militia group are [[Criminal proceedings in the January 6 United States Capitol attack|arrested]] by federal prosecutors for conspiring to [[January 6 United States Capitol attack|breach]] the [[United States Capitol]]. [https://www.nydailynews.com/new-york/ny-virginia-oath-keeper-capitol-20210119-k7qxj7m72vggdii2t5ehposhcm-story.html (''New York Daily News'')] [https://www.cnn.com/2021/01/19/politics/oath-keepers-capitol-riot-charges/index.html (CNN)]
*[[2020 congressional insider trading scandal]]
**The [[United States Department of Justice]] closes an [[insider trading]] probe into [[United States Senate|U.S. Senator]] [[Richard Burr]] of [[North Carolina]] without making him face any criminal charges. [https://www.marketwatch.com/story/feds-wont-charge-sen-richard-burr-with-insider-trading-01611104898# (MarketWatch)]
*[[Protests against Rodrigo Duterte]]
**The [[Philippine]] [[Department of National Defense (Philippines)|Department of National Defense]] terminates a 32-year-old accord with the [[University of the Philippines]], the country's [[national university]], that limits the access of [[Philippine National Police|police]] and [[Armed Forces of the Philippines|military]] personnel into the university's campuses. Faculty members, students, and activists protest the move, calling it "a violation of [[academic freedom]]" and claiming that it would aid the [[Government of the Philippines|government]]'s attempts at [[Red-tagging in the Philippines|red-tagging]] people. [https://www.scmp.com/week-asia/politics/article/3118386/duterte-targets-enemies-state-university-philippines-protests (''South China Morning Post'')]
*A 65-year-old Thai woman is sentenced to 43 years in prison for [[Lèse-majesté in Thailand|insulting the Thai monarchy]] in online posts in 2014. Her sentence, initially for 87 years, was reduced after she pleaded guilty to the charges. It is the longest punishment for ''lèse-majesté'' handed down in Thai history. [https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/world/thai-woman-sentenced-to-43-years-in-jail-for-insulting-monarchy/ar-BB1cSGJO?ocid=uxbndlbing (Reuters on MSN)]
*Bishop [[Daniel Edward Thomas|Daniel Thomas]] of the [[Roman Catholic Diocese of Toledo|Diocese of Toledo]] issues statements on the deaths of a suspect and police officer, and the vandalism and arson at [[Rosary Cathedral (Toledo, Ohio)|Our Lady, Queen of the Most Holy Rosary Cathedral]] in Toledo, Ohio. [https://www.catholicregister.org/home/international/item/32611-ohio-cathedral-vandalism-suspect-police-officer-killed-in-volley-of-gunfire (CNS)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[Internet regulation in Turkey]]
**[[Turkey]]'s [[Information and Communication Technologies Authority (Turkey)|Information and Communication Technologies Authority]] bans [[Advertising|advertisements]] on [[Twitter]], [[Periscope (app)|Periscope]] and [[Pinterest]] after these companies failed to appoint local representatives under a new [[social media]] law. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-turkey-twitter/turkey-slaps-ad-ban-on-twitter-under-new-social-media-law-idUSKBN29O0CT (Reuters)]
*[[Discoveries of exoplanets]]
**Scientists discover that [[WASP-107b]] is a [[super-puff]]. WASP-107b is an [[exoplanet]] the same size as [[Jupiter]] but with one tenth the mass, located 212 light years away from [[Earth]]. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/astronomers-discover-super-puff-gas-giant-exoplanet-wasp-107b-jupiter/ (CBS News)] [http://www.sci-news.com/astronomy/super-puff-exoplanet-wasp-107b-09262.html (Sci-News)]
